source_pr_title: feat(openshift-devenv): restore newest R2 backup into empty PVC via init container
author: amazon-q-developer
body:
:stop_sign: **Security Vulnerability**: Pipeline failure in restore can leave credentials exposed in shell process table and corrupted partial data.

The restore pipeline on line 204 lacks error handling for intermediate pipeline stages. If `aws s3 cp` succeeds but `openssl` decryption or `tar` extraction fails, the staging directory is left with partial data and the marker isn't set, causing infinite retries with the same corrupted stream. Additionally, if the pipeline exits unexpectedly, credentials passed via `env:BACKUP_PASSWORD` remain visible in process listings during the streaming operation.

Add explicit pipeline failure detection with cleanup. The backup script (lines 143-154) demonstrates the correct pattern with rc marker files - use the same approach for the restore pipeline to detect and handle partial failures before they corrupt the staging directory.
```suggestion
    rm -f /tmp/.aws-rc /tmp/.dec-rc /tmp/.tar-rc
    ( aws s3 cp "" - --endpoint-url "${R2_ENDPOINT}" --region auto || echo "$?" > /tmp/.aws-rc ) | ( openssl enc -d -aes-256-cbc -pbkdf2 -pass env:BACKUP_PASSWORD || echo "$?" > /tmp/.dec-rc ) | ( tar xzf - -C "${STAGE}" || echo "$?" > /tmp/.tar-rc ) || pipe_rc=$?
    pipe_rc=${pipe_rc:-0}
    aws_rc=$(cat /tmp/.aws-rc 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
    dec_rc=$(cat /tmp/.dec-rc 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
    tar_rc=$(cat /tmp/.tar-rc 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
    if [ "${aws_rc}" -ne 0 ] || [ "${dec_rc}" -ne 0 ] || [ "${tar_rc}" -ne 0 ] || [ "${pipe_rc}" -ne 0 ]; then
      echo "Fatal: restore pipeline failed (aws_rc=${aws_rc} dec_rc=${dec_rc} tar_rc=${tar_rc} pipe_rc=${pipe_rc})"
      rm -rf "${STAGE}"
      rm -f /tmp/.aws-rc /tmp/.dec-rc /tmp/.tar-rc
      exit 1
    fi
    rm -f /tmp/.aws-rc /tmp/.dec-rc /tmp/.tar-rc
```
